items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: in the first bands that I've organized, Manuel Malo, uh, Leon Malo, uh, had, uh, Frank Christian, uh, Emil Christian, and, uh, uh, uh, I can't think of his other name now. Uh, Charlie Christian.

ctx.x: Well, I'm not sure what you played, but what you played, what you played.

Well, uh, in the first bands that I've organized, Manuel Malo, uh, Leon Malo, uh, had, uh, Frank Christian, uh, Emil Christian, and, uh, uh, uh, I can't think of his other name now. Uh, Charlie Christian. That's right. Charlie Christian. Charlie Christian. And, uh, uh, also, I had, uh, a gentleman, a fellow by the name of Ginnerman, he lived on, uh, Jackson Avenue. Well, of course, there's quite a number of these men.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: The three of the Christians. Frank, too. Frank, Emile, and Charlie.

ctx.x: I was going to ask, what kind of a band did Fisher have? Fisher. Johnny Fisher? Is it a brass band? No, he had an orchestra. Pretty good. It wasn't rag? Pretty good. Pretty good. Chiller used to play with him. Was it ragtime? And this fellow Shannon. This fellow Shannon had with me. He used to play with him too. Fisher had a good band. Was it ragtime? Fisher's band. Ragtime. Yeah. Rag music, yeah. And he used to have, oh, I can't think of his name now. He was on the police a while, playing trombone with him.…
The three of the Christians. Frank, too. Frank, Emile, and Charlie.

Charlie. You know telling them they used to build them short in those days, didn't they? Yeah, they were funny enough. I was thinking, you know, a lot of people had some beautiful con, silver engraved con cornets. I'd sure like to be able to run across some of those. Must be some of them someplace. They are tucked away somewhere. I'd sure like to find a good one. Throw them all over. You see, all this junk is interesting to look at. It is to me. Anything she's, right away, in a book. Yeah, that's good. Right now.…

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

ctx.x: That's Frank Christian there. When do you do that happen, too?
Running back of the wheel. I built that truck you see out there. Yeah, that's Frank Christian, yeah. 36. I built that hook and ladder that's out there.

items.title: Frank Christian Interview, 1965-09-06
items.q: Lane used to get in. Yeah.

ctx.x: He was a good clarinet player. So, actually, probably when you played with Baquet, it was with Papa Lane's band. Yeah.
More than like that. Lane used to get in. Yeah.
Can you tell us about Jimmy Durante? Was he a good pianist? Or how did he play?
